A Schauder regularity theory for nonlocal viscous Hamilton–Jacobi equations
referaty.streszczenie: Viscous Hamilton–Jacobi equations arise as dynamic programming equations in optimal control and differential games, where the unknown function represents the value function of an optimally controlled process. We use a heat-semigroup approach to study the regularity of such equations with nonlocal and mixed local–nonlocal diffusions. Our framework covers a broad class of Lévy-type operators, including fractional Laplacians as well as nonsymmetric and strongly anisotropic operators. Using the Duhamel formulation together with smoothing estimates in Hölder spaces, we obtain optimal spatial Schauder estimates and explicit blow-up rates for higher-order Hölder norms as time approaches zero. referaty.tytul: Local functional equations for polynomials and related topics
referaty.streszczenie: The functional equations for the Riemann zeta function have long been known to admit two classical proofs. One is based on the Mellin transform and an integral representation of the zeta function, while the other relies on Jacobi's theta function. Although these approaches are quite different, they are in fact two manifestations of the same underlying principle: The Poisson summation formula and the self-duality of the Fourier transform. The main theme of this lecture is how this remarkable phenomenon extends to higher dimensions. A successful framework for such a generalization is provided by the theory of prehomogeneous vector spaces, introduced by Mikio Sato. In this talk, I will discuss local functional equations associated with these spaces, the polynomials that satisfy them, and their intimate connections with representation theory, harmonic analysis and number theory, and…

referaty.tytul: Long time behaviour of mean field games with fractional diffusion
referaty.streszczenie: We discuss recent results on the long time behaviour of mean field games systems with fractional diffusion. The dynamics of the players are driven by independent jump processes, controlled through the drift, and confined by an external drift to guarantee ergodicity. In the case of globally Lipschitz, locally uniformly convex Hamiltonians, and weakly coupled and LL monotone costs, we prove that there is a unique solution $(u_T,m_T)$ to the problem in $(0,T)$, and we show that if T is sufficiently large, then $(u_T,m_T)$ satisfies the so-called turnpike property — it is exponentially close to the (unique) stationary ergodic state of the problem.

referaty.tytul: Testowe: Finite-time blow-up versus global existence in a parabolic–elliptic Keller–Segel system with logistic damping
referaty.streszczenie:
We consider the parabolic–elliptic Keller–Segel system with a logistic source $\mu u(1-u)$ in a bounded domain of $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \ge 3$. It is known that for $\mu$ large enough the logistic damping prevents aggregation and all solutions are global and bounded, whereas without it radially symmetric solutions with large mass concentrate in finite time. We show that in the intermediate regime the dichotomy is governed by a critical Morrey-type norm of the initial datum: below a threshold solutions exist globally, while for a class of radial data above it blow-up occurs in finite time, despite the damping. The proofs combine comparison arguments for the cumulated mass function with new weighted energy estimates.

referaty.tytul: Testowe: Conformal prediction for high-dimensional regression with missing covariates
referaty.streszczenie:
Conformal prediction provides prediction intervals with finite-sample coverage guarantees under the sole assumption of exchangeability. In practice, however, covariates are often only partially observed, and the missingness pattern itself carries information about the response. We propose a pattern-adaptive split conformal procedure for sparse high-dimensional regression which combines imputation with reweighting of nonconformity scores within missingness patterns. We prove marginal coverage under missing-at-random mechanisms and approximate coverage conditional on the pattern, and we illustrate the method on simulated data and on a clinical data set with more than 2000 predictors.

referaty.tytul: Testowe: Dimension-free estimates for Riesz transforms in the Laguerre setting
referaty.streszczenie:
We study the vector of Riesz transforms associated with multi-dimensional Laguerre function expansions of Hermite type on $(0,\infty)^d$. Using a bilinear Bellman function adapted to the Laguerre operator together with a suitable semigroup representation, we prove that its $L^p$ norms, $1<p<\infty$, are bounded independently of the dimension $d$ and of the type multi-index $\alpha$ satisfying $\alpha_j \ge -1/2$. We also discuss the sharpness of the resulting constants as $p \to 1$ and possible extensions to the Jacobi setting.

referaty.tytul: Testowe: Boolean cumulants and the Bercovici–Pata bijection for operator-valued distributions
referaty.streszczenie:
The Bercovici–Pata bijection relates infinitely divisible distributions with respect to classical, free and Boolean convolutions and is conveniently expressed in terms of the corresponding cumulants. We present an operator-valued version of the Boolean-to-free part of this bijection, formulated via $B$-valued Boolean and free cumulants and their relation through non-crossing and interval partitions. As an application we obtain new formulas for operator-valued free convolution powers $\mu^{\boxplus t}$ for $t \ge 1$ and describe when these powers are again Boolean infinitely divisible.

referaty.tytul: Testowe: Extremes of Gaussian processes over random time horizons
referaty.streszczenie:
Let $X(t)$ be a centred Gaussian process with stationary increments and let $T$ be a random time independent of $X$. We derive exact asymptotics of $\mathbb{P}\left(\sup_{t \in [0,T]} X(t) > u\right)$ as $u \to \infty$ for a wide class of distributions of $T$, covering both light- and heavy-tailed horizons. The answer exhibits three qualitatively different regimes depending on the interplay between the tail of $T$ and the variance function of $X$. Applications include ruin probabilities in fluid queues with random service interruptions and an extension of the Pickands–Piterbarg constants.
